x: Headline inflation includes food and energy, core inflation leaves out volatile food and fuel, CPI tracks retail prices, and WPI wholesale goods. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Discriminate headline from core inflation.

x: Option C is incorrect: the Labour Bureau compiles CPI-IW. The NSO compiles CPI-Rural, CPI-Urban and CPI-Combined, which the RBI targets.
t: Match each index to the body that compiles it.

x: Both are true: headline inflation swings more than core because it includes food and energy prices, which core leaves out. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the content explains the volatility.

x: A is true and B is false: CPI tracks retail prices of goods and services, but WPI covers only goods, not services.
t: Recall that WPI excludes services.

x: All four are correct: demand-pull comes from rising demand, cost-push from rising costs, bottleneck from supply limits, and stagflation is inflation with slow growth and unemployment.
t: Match each type of inflation to its cause.

x: All three are correct: headline inflation is total inflation, while core inflation shows the underlying trend by leaving out volatile food and fuel.
t: Discriminate headline from core inflation.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Headline inflation represents total inflation.
II. Core inflation indicates the underlying inflation trend.
III. Core inflation excludes volatile food and fuel.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Both are true: inflation is a rise in the general price level, and it reduces what money can buy. R is an effect of inflation, not its definition, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether an effect explains a definition.

x: Both are true: CPI covers goods and services, and CPI-IW is used to revise dearness allowance and wages.
t: Recall what CPI-IW is used for.

x: Both are true: deflation is a fall in prices, and disinflation is a fall in the inflation rate. They are separate ideas, so R does not explain A.
t: Discriminate deflation from disinflation.

x: Both are true: cutting the bank rate adds liquidity, and raising it is contractionary.
t: Follow the bank rate to liquidity.

x: Open market operations, the RBI buying and selling government securities, are a monetary-policy tool. Public revenue belongs to fiscal policy.
t: Discriminate monetary from fiscal tools.

x: Public revenue (taxes and other receipts) is part of fiscal policy, run by the government. OMOs belong to monetary policy.
t: Discriminate monetary from fiscal tools.

x: The UNDP publishes the HDI, Morris D. Morris devised the PQLI, OPHI with the UNDP produces the global MPI, and Welthungerhilfe with Concern Worldwide publishes the Global Hunger Index. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each index to its author.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) HDI
(b) PQLI
(c) MPI
(d) Global Hunger Index

List-II
(i) UNDP
(ii) Morris D. Morris
(iii) OPHI + UNDP
(iv) Welthungerhilfe and Concern Worldwide

Select the correct code:

x: Both are true: the HDI measures human development because it combines health, education and income. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the components explain the measure.

x: Option C is incorrect: IIP measures industrial output (mining, manufacturing, electricity) and is compiled by the NSO. Wholesale prices are WPI, compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser.
t: Match each index to what it measures.

x: All three are correct: the PQLI uses literacy, IMR and life expectancy, the MPI health, education and living standards, and the BNI water, sanitation and housing.
t: Match each index to its components.

x: NITI Aayog publishes the State Health Index, which ranks States on health performance.
t: Match each index to its publisher.

x: The Basic Necessities Index (BNI) appeared in the Economic Survey and covers water, sanitation and housing.
t: Match each index to its publisher.

x: The State Health Index tracks State health performance, CPI retail prices, WPI wholesale prices, and IIP industrial output. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each index to what it measures.

x: Both are true: per capita income focuses on income because income is all it measures. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the content explains the focus.

x: All four are correct: the Gender Inequality Index measures gender inequality across reproductive health, empowerment and the labour market.
t: Recall the three GII dimensions.
s:
Consider the following statements:

I. GII measures gender inequality.
II. GII focuses on gender inequality.
III. GII includes health and empowerment.
IV. GII includes labour.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
